title: Booked for eternity: Ghosts of the Rochester Public Library

content:
Spooky season should not end the moment the clock strikes midnight on Oct. 31. I’m looking at you, stores that have your winter holiday merchandise out in October, and you, television stations that flip from horror to holiday programming pretty much instantaneously.

All I want is to stay among ghosts, ghoulies and goblins just a little bit longer. Which is why I thought it would be fun to spend this week’s column focusing on a haunted New Hampshire library.

Everything you are about to read was conveyed to me by Abby Rosselli, the Rochester Public Library’s programming librarian.

Back in early 2023, the library decided to have Lynne and Willy of Spirit Chasers New England conduct a paranormal investigation of the building. Lynne is a clairvoyant empath, and Willy uses equipment to search for evidence of paranormal activity.

The investigation was prompted by both curiosity and staff members having unexplained experiences. According to Abby, the library’s custodian had reported hearing footsteps and voices several times when she was alone in the building. Her office is in the basement, which is the oldest part of the library.

On another occasion, she came in and heard music blasting from one of the offices. It was the song “Uptown Funk,” and the weirdest part was that the staff member who occupied the office was on vacation. No one had been in there for a few days.

Other staff members had reported feeling unsettled in the basement, sensing a presence standing behind them and even smelling smoke.

The investigation reportedly revealed the presence of three ghosts.

The first was Lillian Parshley, who had been the head librarian for many, many years. She was apparently still there and happy to be at the library.

The second goes by the name of Jonathan and roams the staircase in the original section of the building. He is believed to be a man in his 30s who wears a top hat and simply enjoys being there in the afterlife.

As a matter of fact, when the investigation was over that night, Abby and her boss had to make their rounds to ensure the library was secure and the doors were locked. They were joking around and asked, “Jonathan, is that you?” and the lights turned off on their own.

The final ghost was the not-so-happy spirit of a middle-aged man who seemed grumpy and complained that the librarians were “doing it all wrong.” They suspect he’s the culprit behind the unsettling feelings in the basement. The Rochester librarians aren’t sure who this man is, so they just call him the grumpy man.

While the Leach Library does not have a ghost, and our Halloween programs may be over, we still have plenty of programs to keep you busy in this life and the afterlife!

For adults, we will have a cupcake decorating class on Monday, Nov. 30, at 6:30 p.m. Teens are invited to unleash their creativity at our writers group on Thursday, Nov. 19, at 6 p.m.

Finally, for the smallest members of your family, we have Wiggle Worms Toddler Storytime on Tuesdays and Wednesdays at 10:30 a.m.

To register for any of our events, call 603-432-1132 or email reference@londonderrynh.gov.

Rebecca Berezin is the Senior Reference and Adult Services Librarian at the Leach Library.
